DeleteItemFromArray returns void, so the descriptor reads r=- and the effect shows in sz/doc. The fourth call is on an empty array

the selector reaches a direct child of the root, so the removal surface is exercised on a NON-root container
the witness op on a nested array -- the relink and the cache are per container, not per document
an unresolvable selector leaves no target: every op is a no-op and sz reads -1, distinct from a target of size 0
a selector against an ARRAY root: GetObjectItemCaseSensitive answers NULL, so no target
the selector uses the case-SENSITIVE lookup, so `a` misses `A` -- deliberately fixed so the op's own case flag is the only thing varying
the C would hang a child off the scalar 7 (scalar-parent-child); the driver refuses on BOTH sides so this module's ledger stays on the removal surface. r=0, sz unchanged
the C would give the object a NULL-keyed member printing as ""; same refusal, same reason
the only accepted target: an array. The appended value is CreateNumber of the index field, so it also crosses the negative branch
a document with no program: `init=` alone, and the document must come back untouched
an unrecognized opcode records a `?` step and changes nothing; the next op still runs
opcodes are compared with strcmp, so `DA` is not `da`
ten ops, eight executed: the cap bounds the descriptor whatever the fuzzer sends, and both sides must stop at the same step
a line with no tabs, one tab, two tabs: every missing field reads as empty, so the index is 0 three times
a blank line is a `?` step, not a terminator -- it consumes one of the eight slots
the last op line need not end in a newline
the C copies the op region into a NUL-terminated buffer, so everything past an interior NUL is invisible to it -- one step runs, not three (LESSONS #29). Needs stdin_b64
a non-ASCII key: cJSON compares bytes with strcmp and does no UTF-8 validation, so the raw bytes must match end to end
a key that is not valid UTF-8 at all: it cannot match, but both sides must fail to match it identically rather than one of them replacing bytes
an unparseable document is rc 1 with nothing on stdout: unlike `set`, every op here needs a document to act on
an empty document line is also a parse failure
